q: How do I make a trimmed package from a script?
a: Run `projects.package` with `path` (the project file), `destination` and `"trim": true`. Optionally add `"handles"`: the extra frames kept on each side of every used part (30 by default). MP4 and MOV media are shortened to the parts the sequences use by copying the camera's compressed data, so nothing is re-encoded. The home screen doesn't offer this yet.

q: Can a trimmed package also be a single .revpkg file?
a: Yes. `projects.package` takes both options at once: `"trim": true` shortens the MP4 / MOV media and `"format": "file"` writes one `<project name>.revpkg` (a zip with every file stored as it is) instead of a folder. The receiver uses Import Package (`projects.importPackage`) on that file as usual.

q: Which files does package trimming actually shorten?
a: Only MP4 and MOV media, and only when Revolution can keep their layout exactly. Everything else is copied whole: other formats, and MP4 / MOV files that are fragmented, have several codecs in one track or use complex edit lists.

q: How big will a trimmed package be?
a: Ask first with `projects.package` and `"trim": true, "dryRun": true`: nothing is written and `estimateBytes` gives the bytes that would be copied, with the shortened files counted at the share they keep. The real files can come out bigger than the estimate, because each part starts at the keyframe before it (up to a GOP earlier).

q: If I send a trimmed package, how much room does the other editor have to change the edit?
a: Only what was kept: each used part plus its handles (30 frames on each side by default, more if you set `"handles"` higher), and a part may start up to a GOP earlier because it begins at a keyframe. Anything outside that is not in the package. If they may need to re-cut freely, send a normal package (without `trim`) or raise `handles`.

q: Package the project ~/Videos/FilmCraft Projects/Trip.fcproj to /run/media/usb, trimmed, with two seconds of handles. The footage is 25 fps.
a: Handles are counted in frames, so two seconds at 25 fps is 50. Run `projects.package` with `{"path": "~/Videos/FilmCraft Projects/Trip.fcproj", "destination": "/run/media/usb", "trim": true, "handles": 50}`. It makes `Trip package/` there in the background, with MP4 / MOV media cut to the used parts plus 50 frames each side, nothing re-encoded.

q: Should I trim my packages or send them whole?
a: It depends on what the receiver will do. Trimming (`projects.package` with `"trim": true`) makes a package much smaller when you used little of long clips, with identical quality since nothing is re-encoded; good for sending a finished edit for colour, sound or review over a slow link. The costs: the receiver can only re-cut inside the kept parts and handles, proxies of shortened clips are left out (they make new ones after import), and some MP4 / MOV layouts are copied whole anyway. A whole package is bigger but leaves every frame available, which suits handing a project to another editor to keep cutting.

q: The proxies of a trimmed package are missing after import. What now?
a: That's expected: proxies of shortened media are left out of a trimmed package, because they no longer line up with the cut files. Make new proxies from the imported media. Proxies of clips that were copied whole come along when the package was made with `"proxies": true`.
